#[export] Program Instance iso_equivalence : Equivalence Isomorphism := { Equivalence_Reflexive := @iso_id; Equivalence_Symmetric := @iso_sym; Equivalence_Transitive := fun _ _ _ g f => iso_compose f g }.

statement_record.book: An equivalence relation on a set A is a binary relation ~ on A satisfying: a ~ a for all a (reflexivity); a ~ b iff b ~ a (symmetry); a ~ b and b ~ c imply a ~ c (transitivity).
statement_record.intree: Class Setoid A := { equiv : crelation A; setoid_equiv : Equivalence equiv } — and, as a worked assertion that a given binary relation satisfies exactly the three laws, `Program Instance iso_equivalence : Equivalence Isomorphism := { Equivalence_Reflexive := @iso_id; Equivalence_Symmetric := @iso_sym; Equivalence_Transitive := … }`.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same three laws. Two presentation differences, neither weakening: (i) the library packages carrier-plus-chosen-relation as one structure (a Setoid) rather than a property of a given relation, but the bare property is available as `Equivalence R` for any R (Coq's Type-valued CRelationClasses, re-exported through Lib/Foundation.v:2 CMorphisms) and is asserted in-tree of concrete relations — iso_equivalence above, Quotient_equivalence at Construction/Quotient.v:241, and every `homset` field of a Category; (ii) `equiv : crelation A` is Type-valued, i.e. proof-relevant, so the relation is not literally a subset of A × A (Lib/Setoid.v's header says this is deliberate, so equivalence proofs may carry computational content) — a strengthening in data, harmless for the definition. In-tree symmetry is the single implication a ≈ b → b ≈ a, equivalent to the book's biconditional. This is the library's foundational structure: every hom is a setoid, so morphism equality throughout is a chosen equivalence relation.

statement_record.book: A function S → T is a subset F ⊆ S × T such that for every s ∈ S there is a UNIQUE t ∈ T with (s,t) ∈ F; notation F(s) = t. For t ∈ T the preimage of t is { s ∈ S | F(s) = t }. F is surjective when every t has some s with F(s) = t; injective when F(s₁) = F(s₂) forces s₁ = s₂; bijective when both.
statement_record.intree: `Class injective … := { inj {x y} : f x ≈ f y -> x ≈ y }`; `Class surjective … := { surj {y} : { x & f x ≈ y} }`; `Lemma bijective_is_iso {A B : SetoidObject} (h : A ~{Sets}~> B) : injective h -> surjective h -> IsIsomorphism h`; `Record SetoidMorphism … := { morphism :> x → y; proper_morphism :> Proper (respectful equiv equiv) morphism }`; `Definition sub_reindex {x y : C} (f : y ~> x) (u : SubObj x) : SubObj y := …` (preimage of a subobject along f, via the chosen pullback).
statement_record.strength_comparison: Injectivity and surjectivity are faithful setoid rephrasings (≈ for =); `surjective`'s chosen preimage `{ x & f x ≈ y }` is exactly the constructive existential, since in this library ∃ IS sigT (Lib/Foundation.v:61), so it is not a hidden strengthening. Bijectivity appears only as the conjunction of hypotheses of bijective_is_iso, which additionally supplies the inverse function with no appeal to choice. Functions are primitive (a Coq function plus a respectfulness certificate), NOT defined relationally: only the forward direction functions → relations is formalized, as `Program Instance Relation_Functor : Coq ⟶ Rel` sending f to its graph (Instance/Rel.v:167). intree-weaker on preimage: sub_reindex is the preimage of a SUBOBJECT along a morphism and needs chosen pullbacks; the book's element-indexed fibre is not it. The concrete-instance companions are Instance/Sets.v:369 injectivity_is_monic (injective ↔ Monic, an iff) and Instance/FinSet/Classifier.v:335 finset_monic_iff_injective.

gap: Three specific pieces are missing. (1) The relational definition of a function is absent: there is no predicate 'F ⊆ S × T is total and single-valued' and no theorem that such an F yields a function — greps for 'functional', 'single-valued', 'graph' turn up only Instance/Rel.v:167 Relation_Functor (functions → relations, the converse direction only). (2) The preimage of an ELEMENT, f⁻¹(t) = { s | f s ≈ t }, is defined nowhere; the nearest in-tree constructions are sub_reindex (preimage of a subobject, requiring HasPullbacks), the image `Sets_Image := ∃ y : Y, ∃ x : X, f x ≈ y` (Instance/Sets/Image.v:75) and char_setoid's image predicate `λ b, ∃ a, m a ≈ b` (Instance/Sets/Classifier.v:186) — all image-side, not fibre-side. (3) `bijective` is not a named predicate; the notion exists only as the two hypotheses of bijective_is_iso, and the converse (an iso of Sets is injective and surjective) is not stated.

STRENGTH_COMPARISON CORRECTION (does not change the classification, so no field overwrite): the record asserts that `surjective`'s `{ x & f x ~~ y }` 'is exactly the constructive existential, since in this library ~E IS sigT (Lib/Foundation.v:61), so it is not a hidden strengthening'. The notation chain is real (Lib/Foundation.v:61 binds 'exists' to sigT and :66 routes the Unicode existential through it), but the conclusion understates the difference AGAINST THE BOOK: relative to Seven Sketches' plain 'for every t there exists s', the in-tree class is SPLIT surjectivity, and the library itself says so twice -- Lib/Setoid.v:120 '[f] is (split) surjective: every [y] has a chosen preimage up to ~~' and Theory/Equivalence.v:38-40 'stated in the split, choice-carrying house style ... the split [surjective] class of Lib/Setoid.v'. Corollary id_monic : ∀ x, Monic (id (x:=x)).  …  Corollary id_epic : ∀ x, Epic (id (x:=x)).  (line 142)

statement_record.book: For any set X the identity function id_X sends each element to itself, and it is bijective.
statement_record.intree: `Program Instance iso_id {x : C} : x ≅ x := { to := id; from := id }` (so in Sets the identity setoid map has a two-sided inverse), `Corollary id_monic : ∀ x, Monic (id (x:=x))` and `Corollary id_epic : ∀ x, Epic (id (x:=x))`, over `Definition setoid_morphism_id {x : SetoidObject} : SetoidMorphism x x := {| morphism := Datatypes.id |}`.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same in substance. The in-tree form is categorical: the identity is an isomorphism in ANY category (iso_id), hence in Sets, where an isomorphism is a two-sided-inverse bijection of setoids — the same notion the library uses for bijection (bijective_is_iso, Instance/Sets.v:400). The elementwise injective half is moreover immediate from id_monic through the iff injectivity_is_monic (Instance/Sets.v:369). intree-weaker only in phrasing: no lemma literally reads `injective (id) ∧ surjective (id)`, and the converse iso → injective ∧ surjective is not stated in-tree (only bijective → iso is), so the elementwise reading is one trivial step away rather than transcribed.

Citations verified line-exact: Theory/Isomorphism.v:149 `#[export] Program Instance iso_id {x : C} : x ~= x`, Theory/Morphisms.v:135 `Corollary id_monic : forall x, Monic (id (x:=x))` and :142 `Corollary id_epic`, Instance/Sets.v:155 `Definition setoid_morphism_id@{o h p} {x : SetoidObject@{o p}} : SetoidMorphism@{o h p} x x := {| morphism := Datatypes.id |}`. PRESENT still holds under the frozen definition: the identity morphism is primitive (Theory/Category.v:118), it is an isomorphism in every category, and in Sets an isomorphism is precisely the library's own notion of bijection (bijective_is_iso), so the item is formalized in substance with only a phrasing gap.
